title: The Portrait of Harrow Glen
premise: Casper Yarrow, a pest controller with fifteen years of rational explanations behind her, is called to Harrow Glen, a decaying house where every mirror reflects the room one second late. The delay widens each night, and what the mirrors show her is a household that existed in 1974 — a family that took something from the house and paid for it by being folded into its walls. To escape, Casper must find what was taken, return it to the place it was stolen from, and accept that the house demands a keeper in exchange; she survives only by choosing to stay bound to Harrow Glen, trading her freedom for the release of everyone else.
about_author: Sebastian Vane is the pen name of a former building surveyor who spent a decade cataloguing the strange histories of English country houses before turning those case notes into fiction. They write horror about places that remember, and they still refuse to work in houses with more than one staircase.

chapters.title: The Call-Out
chapters.summary: POV Casper. A routine job at Harrow Glen: scratching in the walls, droppings that aren't droppings. Casper finds greasy handprints on the inside of sealed wall cavities, five-fingered, human-sized. She tells herself raccoons, though none live here. Emotional beat: professional calm stretched thin over old unease.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Returning at dusk to finish the job, she notices the hallway mirror lags — her reflection moves a beat behind. Every reflective surface in the house does it. In the lag, something stands beside her reflection that isn't there when she turns. Beat: dread arriving through the most mundane detail.

chapters.title: The House That Wasn't Sold
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Researching at the county records office, she learns Harrow Glen's last sale was 1974 — to the Merrick family, who never appear in any later document. No deaths recorded, no move. The house has simply sat, taxes unpaid, unclaimed. Beat: the first crack in her rational worldview.

chapters.title: Scratching Back
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Overnight stakeout with cameras. The scratching answers her knocking — three raps, then three back. On camera, the wall bulges outward like skin under pressure. She flees but leaves her toolbag; by morning it sits neatly on the porch, every tool cleaned and arranged. Beat: terror mixed with horrible courtesy.

chapters.title: What the Mirrors Keep
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The lag stretches to four seconds. In the delayed reflections she sees the house furnished as it was in 1974, warm-lit, occupied. A woman in the glass mouths words Casper can't decode. When Casper smashes one mirror, all of them bleed light instead of shattering. Beat: escalation and helplessness.

chapters.title: The Neighbor Who Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Elderly neighbor Edith Tolliver, three doors down, recognizes the name Yarrow on the van and goes pale. Her sister did Casper's mother's books; the Yarrows lived here once too. Edith warns: 'It doesn't take people. It takes people who owe.' Beat: personal history entangling with the haunting.

POV alternating Casper/dream-Merrick. Asleep in her van outside the house, Casper dreams the Merrick family's last evening — dinner, laughter, a father burying something beneath the cellar floor while his wife weeps. She wakes with dirt under her fingernails. Beat: the past reaching forward through her body.

chapters.title: Inside the Walls
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Investigating the cavity, she finds the walls hollowed into corridors wider than the house's footprint allows. Scratched into the plaster: hundreds of tally marks, and names — including YARROW. Something moves parallel to her, matching her steps. Beat: claustrophobia and the revelation she was always expected.

chapters.title: Edith's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Edith (one chapter). 1974 flashback: young Edith watched the Merricks' son dig up the cellar floor and carry out a small iron box. The family vanished within the week. Edith's own mother helped them hide it and spent her remaining years listening to walls. Beat: guilt inherited like furniture.

chapters.title: The Second Delay
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The mirror lag reaches ten seconds — long enough for the reflected room to show events that haven't happened yet. She watches her own reflection sit down heavily, defeated, hours before she feels that way. The house isn't showing the past anymore. Beat: time itself becoming hostile.

chapters.title: Digging
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Following the dream, she breaks the cellar floor and finds the empty cavity shaped exactly like an iron box, lined with claw marks on the inside. Whatever was buried got out — or was let out. Above her, every door in the house opens at once. Beat: the mystery inverting; the theft freed something.

chapters.title: The Thing With Fingerprints
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Night. The prints in the walls are fresh again, leading downward now. She follows them to the cellar and meets it: a figure assembled from the missing Merricks, moving with borrowed gestures, wearing the father's smile wrong. It doesn't attack. It asks, politely, if she's brought it home. Beat: confrontation without violence — persuasion as horror.

chapters.title: Bargaining With Walls
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The entity explains the terms: the box held the house's heart, taken by a previous owner in 1961; the Merricks stole it back and hid it badly; the house consumed them as payment. Return the box to where it was taken from, and everyone goes free — except whoever carries it, who becomes the new keeper. Beat: the price made explicit.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: POV Casper. She runs. Drives two hundred miles, checks into a motel, and finds the bathroom mirror already lagging. The lag follows her now — she's been marked since she touched the tally marks. Her reflection starts acting independently, packing a bag, driving back. Beat: there is no outside anymore.

chapters.title: Edith's Box
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Edith, dying, gives her the iron box her mother kept hidden for fifty years — the house's heart, cold and humming. Inside: not treasure but a ledger of every soul the house has held, pages still blank, waiting. Edith dies at peace, finally unburdened. Beat: inheritance accepted.

chapters.title: The Long Corridor
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Carrying the box, she re-enters Harrow Glen. The interior has rearranged into a single corridor stretching impossibly, lined with doors, behind which she hears the Merricks living their 1974 evening on loop. The walls whisper her mother's name. Beat: the gauntlet begins; grief weaponized.

chapters.title: Doors
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Each door offers her a life: staying, belonging, being known — the things she's starved for. Behind one, her mother waits at a kitchen table. Casper nearly opens it; the reflection in the door's brass handle shows the truth — her mother's chair is empty, always was. Beat: temptation and the theme of belonging confronted.

chapters.title: Where It Was Taken
chapters.summary: POV Casper. At the corridor's end: the original hearth, bricked over in 1961, the true center of the house. The entity blocks her path, offering one final trade — put down the box, walk away, and it will keep the Merricks comfortable forever. Comfort as damnation. Beat: climax threshold.

chapters.title: The Return
chapters.summary: POV Casper. She fights through — not with strength but by naming the dead, reading the ledger aloud, giving each trapped soul their name back until the entity unravels into five separate grieving people. She sets the box in the hearth. The house exhales. The mirrors align to real time. Beat: climax; power dissolved by witness, not force.

chapters.title: Keeper
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The Merricks step free, aged a single evening across fifty years, and leave without looking back. The house settles around Casper — doors closing gently, warmth returning, the tally marks adding one new name. She understands the trade she made and finds, terrifyingly, that part of her wanted it. Beat: the cost paid; ambivalence honored.

chapters.title: Explanations
chapters.summary: POV Casper, months later. She runs her pest control business from Harrow Glen now, taking calls about noises in walls across the county — and knowing which ones are real. She writes to Edith's grave weekly. The mirrors show the rooms exactly on time, except one, in the cellar, which shows tomorrow. Beat: resolution with a held breath.

chapters.title: The New Call-Out
chapters.summary: POV Casper. A letter arrives: another house, another family hearing fingerprints. The ledger's next page has begun writing itself in ink she didn't provide. Casper packs her tools, checks the cellar mirror one last time — her reflection nods before she does — and drives toward the next debt. Beat: cyclical ending; survival continues, and so does the price.
